title: I'm making a Pokémon/ temtem-inspired educational online game — here's the trailer and a look at the new creature designs
author: Jeckyll25
selftext:
I'm currently working on Grammons (Grammar Monsters). The idea is to collect different creatures, put together a team of three and battle other teams. Have a look at the trailer to see the gameplay!

It's being built as an online game where you can see other players in the world and challenge them to duels. So you'll be able to try out your team against other people's combinations, too.

Each Grammon has its own combination of elements, categories and abilities. Catching a new Grammon unlocks its skills, which you can then teach to other Grammons of the same element, with a few exceptions. So catching new creatures also opens up more options for the team you already have. Combined with ability upgrades, this gives you lots of room to experiment and build a team around the moves and combinations you enjoy.

The educational part is English grammar. You complete grammar challenges to unlock abilities and upgrade them. **This happens outside of battles.** Once you're in a fight, it's about choosing your moves and working with your team—there are no grammar questions popping up between attacks. I wanted learning to be part of how you develop your creatures, while letting the battles play out as a game.

I've also been working on a visual overhaul. The before-and-after image in the comments shows Cindervix, Rillfin, Spriglet and Zephyrel. I wanted to keep the blocky style but give them more personality and make each one feel more distinct. Pretty happy with how they're coming along!

What do you think of the new designs? And how does that separation between learning and battling sound to you?
